full_judgment:
4. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge, the Defendants (heirs of original Defendant no. 1) preferred an appeal. The learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court allowed, the appeal and dismissed the suit giving his own reasoning’s. He found that the lease by Abdul Aziz in favour of Hazi Abdus Sattar by Kobulyat Ext A and subsequent Kabuliyats as alleged by the Defendants were true and genuine and they were acted upon. Although there was no Patta made in pursuance of Kabuliat or any rent receipt produced by the Defendants, the learned Additional District Judge observed:- 

 8. Mr. Dewan A.M.S. Zaman next alleged that kobulyat Ext. A being a unilateral document not followed by patta or rent receipt, the learned Additional District Judge has erred in law in not holding that it did not create any lease of the suit land. He has submitted that the learned Additional District Judge should have held that kabala Ext A was never acted upon. He has further submitted that even if it be admitted for the sake of argument that a lease was created by Ext A, the same ended with the expiry of three years from the date of Ext. A. Mr. Zaman ultimately argued that the learned Additional District Judge had erred in law in finding the possession of the Defendants in plot No. 951 only on the basis of the inspection report and the learned Additional District Judge should have found that the Plaintiff had possession in plot No. 951 which is attracted by the boundary given in the Plaintiffs, kabala Ext 2-2(b) and their predecessor's kabala, 2c. 

 10. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions of the learned Advocates for both sides. It is clear from the judgment of the learned Additional District Judge that he has made certain surmises in course of his judgment. His surmises have no basis. These are with regard to the payment of rent on the basis of Ext. A and also with regard to heirs and female co-sharers possessing their ancestral land. The learned Additional District Judge has also not adverted to certain important aspects of the case considered by the learned trial Court. In particular, he has not adverted to the fact that Defdt. No. 1 Abdus Sattar, the father-in-law of Sayed Moula Ali himself had written the kabala Ext. 2C which shows transfer of khas land and not of superior interest. The learned Additional District Judge has also not sufficiently explained the absence of Dakhila and Patta in pursuance of Ext A, but the absence of those documents had weighed with the learned Subordinate Judge who tried the suit. In these circumstances. I am of the opinion that the appellate Court's judgment was not a proper judgment of reversal.
